concepts.label: cbrecovery
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the command-line tool that retrieves data lost from a local cluster (following multi-node failure) back FROM a remote XDCR-replicated bucket, reversing the normal source-to-target flow. First contact anywhere in the corpus. Sibling of the promoted tool:cbbackupmgr family, but structurally different: cbrecovery reads from a live, remote XDCR target rather than from a backup archive, and is meaningful only in the presence of a pre-existing XDCR replication.

notable_absence.predicate: requiresPriorExecutionOf / hasExecutionConstraint (ordering, not found to fit cleanly)
notable_absence.finding: The page states a real and important ordering constraint - rebalance must NOT be run before cbrecovery, because rebalancing affects local vBucket data and would prevent recovery ('_Do not_ at this point rebalance the cluster...Rebalance will be performed _after_ the lost data has been recovered') - but every existing ordering predicate in the registry (requiresPriorExecutionOf) is phrased as 'X depends on Y having already run', the opposite direction from 'Y must NOT run until X has'. Rather than force this onto requiresPriorExecutionOf backwards or mint a new predicate for a single occurrence, the constraint is recorded here in prose only.

cross_component_finding: cbrecovery IS THE ONLY TOOL IN THIS BATCH THAT READS AGAINST THE REPLICATION DIRECTION RATHER THAN WITH IT. Every other mechanism in this batch (create/pause/resume/filter/scopes-and-collections) operates source-to-target, the direction XDCR itself replicates in; cbrecovery is invoked on the SOURCE cluster but pulls data FROM the target, deliberately reversing the flow to recover from local data loss. No reference-tree or Capella page describes this reversed-flow use of an existing replication at all - Capella's own disaster-recovery story (out of this batch) is presumably backup/restore-based rather than XDCR-based, since Capella clusters do not expose a CLI-tool surface comparable to cbrecovery.
